Episode 119. Banquet at Geomhwang Fortress (6)
The central arena of Geomhwang Fortress was known to be the largest in the world.
It was a place that could not be visited unless you were a member of the Hairan family.
The foreigners who entered the arena were taken aback by its incredibly vast and extensive size.
In the middle of the arena, Hairan's knights were lined up.
As Ron signaled, the knights separated to both sides, blocking the spectators' seats.
The spectator seats were quickly and orderly filling up.
Jin and Lata faced each other in the middle of the arena, with Ron taking a place between them.
Although so many people were gathered, not even a breath could be heard. Everyone was simply hoping for their favorite character to win.
"Lata Proch, Jin Runcandel."
"Yes, Lord Ron."
"Yes."
"I don't know the background between the two of you. However, as a senior warrior and as the master of Geomhwang Fortress, I must give you one piece of advice."
"Please tell us."
"Never try to cripple or kill your opponent. Anyone who breaks this rule will have to face my sword directly."
It was essentially a message for Lata. Even those who did not know the situation between them could tell that Lata was showing one-sided hostility.
Killing at a banquet was strictly forbidden even at Runcandel's outcast party.
"I will keep that in mind."
"There will be glory for the winner and learning for the loser. I expect a great fight worthy of my grandson and the people gathered here."
As Ron stepped back towards the spectator seats, a knight struck a huge drum on one side of the arena with great force.
Boom-!
It was the signal to start the duel. And before the drum sound even faded away, Lata made the first move.
Like Fey, he was also using twin swords.
Swoosh-!
Two blades and Sigmund intertwined, creating a deafening clash.
'I expected it, but it's quite heavy.'
Cracks appeared on the solid ground where the two were standing. Those among the spectators who didn't expect such a strong offense and defense that could break the arena were quite surprised.
"I thought you would yield the first move since you are a senior and have a higher reputation."
"I don't like you enough to show such generosity."
Jin smirked.
"Well, if we look at it purely from the standpoint of martial arts, disregarding seniority and reputation, this is the right picture."
Lata couldn't be entirely angry at those words.
He felt it as soon as their swords crossed.
'The rumor that he caused a commotion in the Sword Garden... it wasn't a lie.'
The twin blades of the 'Ghost' sword trembled with the immense energy that Jin possessed. A shiver ran down Lata's back, originating from the trembling of the Sword Spirit.
He was strong.
Lata had originally thought that Jin had survived out of luck, or perhaps his subordinates had made some mistake.
Even if his younger brother had secretly participated in the mission, Lata had believed that there was no chance of failure since 'Grimol' was guarding his side.
But it wasn't the case.
'From the beginning, I should have directly engaged him with my direct subordinates or formed a team with only captains like Grimol.'
He underestimated the weight of the name 'Twelfth Generation'.
Although it wasn't widely known, Lata had once fought and won against another member of Runcandel.
Bang, crash, crack!
The three swords continued to clash, creating explosive sounds.
Jin was strong, Lata admitted, but his anger had not subsided.
Furthermore, he still believed that he could not lose to Jin. Lata had also defeated numerous strong opponents he had met so far, every single time without fail.
Even those who seemed absolutely unbeatable eventually fell to their knees. The future of the Twelfth Generation of Runcandel in front of him wouldn't be any different.
On the other hand, Jin couldn't feel such intense emotions while facing Lata.
Even considering Ron's strict order not to kill the opponent, Lata's sword didn't feel very threatening. This was despite the twin swords constantly brushing past his face and stabbing near his ears.
'...Have I only fought against strong opponents lately?'
It had been less than a month since he had fought with all his strength against the entire Runcandel.
In that fight, Jin had survived near-death experiences multiple times, which meant he had overcome the wall of growth.
In other words,
Jin's sword had become even more mature than before. It contained insights that couldn't be achieved at his age, and depths that even those who had reached the pinnacle couldn't easily read.
It seemed as if he could foresee the trajectory of Lata's sword.
"It seems like the Twelfth Generation of Runcandel is being pushed back."
"It's still too early to surpass the Ghost Captain."
Those who hadn't reached the pinnacle made such predictions.
However, the warriors who accurately grasped the flow of the battle barely managed to hide their astonishment.
"Is he really the Twelfth Generation?"
"At this rate, the Ghost Captain will definitely be defeated."
Amid the conflicting evaluations, Ron was confident.
He thought that Jin and Lata were already living in different worlds.
'That devilish guy has already reached the ranks of superhumans... The Ghost Captain has quite an impressive potential, but he's still in the world of ordinary people.'
The strongest of the ordinary, the weakest of the superhuman.
That was the kind of battle it was. Although it appeared as if Jin was stepping back, it wasn't because he was being overwhelmed, but because he could afford to handle the attacks so leisurely.
Ron turned his head and looked at his grandson.
As expected, Dante seemed almost entranced, as if he had encountered a divine being.
'Although one might feel jealous or competitive, could it be that I'm just excited about the achievements of my friend?'
It was an odd feeling.
Dante was thought to be the only person in the world who looked at him with such eyes. Indeed, during their childhood, Dante had always looked up to Ron like that.
He had considered him the final destination he would eventually reach.
At that moment, however, Ron suddenly realized the most significant difference between Dante and Jin.
'Jin Runcandel, that devil, unlike my lovely grandson...'
There is no final destination for him.
He must have perceived his father, Chiron Runcandel, the world's strongest knight, as just one 'wall' to overcome.
He must believe that the pinnacle he has to reach lies somewhere beyond that.
At the realization of that fact, chills ran down his spine.
It had been a long time since he felt such an emotion while watching someone else's fight.
Squeak-!
Suddenly, blood sprayed through the air.
It was Jin's blood. The Twinblade Ghost had cut Jin's hand. If the cut had been just a bit deeper, his hand would have been severed.
Jin hastily put some distance between them.
That's how it appeared in Lata's eyes.
'Shouldn't you have pushed in and gambled for a win, 12th generation?!'
The Twinblade Ghost fell at an angle. It seemed that Jin, whose stance had already been disrupted, wouldn't be able to dodge the attack.
It cut.
No, it should have cut. When the Twinblade Ghost scraped the air, Lata felt as if the world's clock had stopped for a moment.
'It's not there, even though it was the perfect distance...!'
The next moment, Lata saw a single point in his vision.
It was the tip of Jin's sword. He couldn't understand when Jin had made such a fierce thrust.
A droplet of blood splattered from Lata's cheek. He had turned his head just before Sigmund struck, avoiding injury.
That evasion was also a feat only possible by a warrior like Lata.
But Lata knew.
'He purposely aimed for my face, so I could avoid a fatal blow.'
In a fight, the face is naturally one of the worst vital points.
However, it is also one of the easiest body parts to protect. By simply turning one's head or slightly ducking, most attacks aimed at the face can be avoided.
Therefore, many fights between warriors ended with fatal injuries to other parts of the body rather than the neck or face.
If Jin had aimed for the heart instead of the face, Lata would have suffered a significant injury that would have forced him to give up regardless of his response.
Gritting his teeth...!
Lata trembled with humiliation.
"Do it properly, Jin Runcandel."
"What's the problem this time?"
"Purposely aiming for the face..."
"I aimed for the face because I judged it to be safer than other areas. If I had targeted the heart or abdomen, Lata would have retaliated even at the risk of death."
It was not a lie.
If that had happened, Jin might have been injured as well, and one of them would have inevitably died or suffered a similar fate.
"If I do it properly, Lata cannot survive."
Annoyingly, Lata did not hear that as 'arrogant.' It just sounded like a natural assessment from a person who was clearly stronger than himself.
"At least that's the case in this arena. If this were a battlefield or my bedchamber, the story might be different."
The purpose of the Ghost Brigade is not for knights to engage in one-on-one duels.
A mercenary group specialized in dealing with stronger opponents more efficiently. Lata was their leader.
That didn't mean their individual combat ability was lacking, but there was no helping it if the opponent was formidable.
For a while, the two stood silently, staring at each other.
Some spectators interpreted it as a new reconnaissance battle, while others saw it as the silence of acknowledging victory and defeat.
And Lata felt ashamed.
It was not the shame of being defeated. Nor was it the shame of not recognizing the opponent's skills and picking a fight like a thunderstruck fool.
It was simply the shame of realizing that he was of a smaller caliber than the young man before him.
Jin had saved his younger brother who came as an assassin, and to this day, he hasn't made any excessive demands of Lata.
Lata had barked like a frightened dog in his desperation to reclaim his brother.
In the midst of the silence,
Jin suddenly felt an immense energy emanating from Lata.
'His eyes showed acceptance of victory and defeat?'
Lata was thinking the same thing. He thought that a dangerous energy was extending from Jin, not himself.
So Lata was about to say, with the heart of a warrior who accepts the outcome, that he should cut one part of his body.
It was natural for Jin to be angry, he thought.
But that dangerous energy was neither Jin's nor Lata's.
It was starting right beneath their feet.
"Get back!"
"Move away!"
Realizing the truth, both shouted at the same time.
The next moment, the arena floor split entirely, and something enormous shot up. Ron had already drawn his sword and was prepared to counter it.
